title: The queen and the king
outcomes: Taps every square a queen can reach
Knows the king may never step onto an attacked square or next to the enemy king
Tells which of the pieces on the board can reach or capture on a square

steps.text: The **queen** is the strongest piece. She moves like a rook and a bishop combined: any distance along a rank, a file or a diagonal. She cannot jump, and she captures the same way: by landing on an enemy piece.

steps.caption: Eight directions. Two white pawns and two black pawns decide where each line stops.

steps.text: The **king** moves one square in any direction. He is the piece you must never lose, so there is one extra rule: **a king may never move onto a square the enemy attacks** (a square where an enemy piece could capture). That also means two kings can never stand on neighbouring squares.

steps.caption: The black rook attacks the whole fifth rank. The king cannot step onto it.

steps.text: The king can capture too, but only if the piece is not guarded. A piece is **guarded** (or defended) when a friendly piece could recapture on its square. Ask before you capture: which enemy pieces attack the square I am about to land on?

steps.title: Same capture, one change
steps.prompt: A black pawn appears on c6. Predict first: can the king still take the knight?
